items.title: Isaiah Morgan Interview, 1958-12-01
items.q: Now I don't know why they, now Howard is another one. He's been playing a whole lot of stuff for Jim.

ctx.x: Well anyway, he was teaching them. And I don't tell you the facts, I don't know if any of them was reading at that time.

And because my brother Sam, he read when he was up here, I don't know what he did in the country, see. Me and Sam used to put them old hard numbers on us up there on the Estory Garden, I heard Al speaking about the Estory. He bring them numbers right there and let that place get full of people and then he'd draw them out there. Put them up there. But you hadn't rehearsed even? No, he said, who fall down, stay down. See I can't get you all to rehearse. Miss Trombone, Sally Trombone, all that's for trombone work.…

And I don't see why they turned that way. And I don't see why they turned anymore. I think he couldn't travel or something. Maybe I think he had a job here and they went on the road. Alvin didn't want to go on the road or something.

items.title: Avery "Kid" Howard Interview, 1961-05-22
items.q: And so finally one night, Young Morgan's band, he had his on band at that particular time, and I went to a party and the drummer got hooked.

ctx.x: On drums? No. Well that was something that went about that I said I couldn't play, which I couldn't. I did many times go to parties. And so finally one night, Young Morgan's band, he had his on band at that particular time, and I went to a party and the drummer got hooked. And so when I walked in, they said, well here come a drummer. Well I couldn't get up and I went up and played with him. Jim Robinson was with Young Morgan at that particular time. And then Andrew Morgan came in and they liked what I was doing…

items.title: Avery "Kid" Howard Interview, 1958-12-22
items.q: And then we, when I'd taken up with Isley Morgan, they had a truck.

ctx.x: How did you travel usually in the United States? Well, we had cars.

People had some of those type of cars. Yeah cars, you see. All we would have we'd rent them, see. Yeah. Rent the cars. And then we, when I'd taken up with Isley Morgan, they had a truck. We'd just travel the truck. Couldn't go. It was 25 miles an hour.

But we were slow by the show. Well I'd have to sit in the back of the truck then. Yeah, we'd be in the back of the truck. And just go on the road. Let's see if there's anything else about the dance halls we could talk about. About how many girls did they usually hire there?
